correctness.rationale: Starting from the killed Brownian kernel and stationary renewal mixture, integrate positions below L-a_iR to get the joint event integral. Under w=R/sqrt(4Dt) the N probability factors each yield a factor L/R; a w^(N-3)exp(-B w²/4) majorant for fixed B=sum a_i²>0 is integrable for N>2. The gamma integral gives exact C_N B^(-(N-2)/2) power-law amplitude; conditioning yields v=4DA/R² with inverse-gamma shape (N-2)/2 and scale B. For mixed nonnegative powers the Rayleigh limit of each conditional surviving distance is (4Dt)^(p_i/2)*Gamma(1+p_i/2), so the positive age integrand at infinity is t^((sum p_i-N)/2), integrable precisely for sum p_i<N-2, with log divergence at equality. Independently checked amplitude normalization against the published exact gamma-law source using T=L² tau_N/D, and verified its reciprocal clock transformation; infinite assertions rest on the explicit integrability proof.

Its theorem already gives for all k and a_i>0 the identical joint far-left orthant asymptotic and constant, k^(-(N-2)/2) dependence, conditional Gamma clock U=R²/(4DA) for a one-particle extreme, the exact marginal moment cutoff q<N-2, and covariance consequences. The submitted Y_i=L-X_i thresholds differ by a fixed shift and have the same leading limit; C_N and K_N are algebraically identical after L scaling. The submitted inverse-gamma age is the reciprocal of the published Gamma clock, extended to joint thresholds by the same published multivariate limit proof. Its summed mixed-moment cutoff is the standard conditional-independence power test with the published renewal-age asymptotic, not an independent nonstandard theorem.
